data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between competing accounts of a sudden rise in a school's standardized test scores, where one explanation credits instructional reform and the other points to irregularities in test administration?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Right-to-wrong erasures outnumber wrong-to-right erasures on legitimately completed answer sheets.
  • Erasure analysis identifies with certainty which individual student altered each answer.
data.a_html:
Competing explanations of an abrupt score jump are adjudicated not by weighing their plausibility in the abstract, but by deriving from each a distinct set of observable consequences and testing the forensic record against them. Genuine instructional reform predicts gains distributed across items roughly in proportion to item difficulty, visible in classroom work, and sustained in later cohorts; irregular administration predicts signatures in the answer documents themselves. Lincoln Elementary's fifth-grade math proficiency rate rose from 38 percent to 81 percent in a single year, and that forty-three-point jump is precisely the evidence that showed the state testing agency it was dealing with a statistical outlier, which is how the agency flagged the school's one-year score gain. The state released anonymized answer-sheet and item-response data to the research team.

Erasure analysis measures the rate of wrong-to-right answer changes on scanned answer sheets. Lincoln Elementary's wrong-to-right erasure rate exceeded the state mean by more than five standard deviations, whereas on legitimately completed answer sheets right-to-wrong erasures outnumber wrong-to-right erasures. Erasure analysis identifies with certainty which individual student altered each answer, a property that cannot be squared with the technique's being no more than a measure of wrong-to-right change rates across a scanned document; an aggregate rate attaches to a sheet of paper, not to a culprit.

Item-level response patterns showed implausibly high accuracy on the most difficult test items, which is the trace a transcription of correct answers leaves behind rather than the profile incremental teaching gains produce. That statistical work was finished before any witness was questioned. Investigators interviewed teachers and proctors who were present during the test administration, and as a result four teachers reported that completed answer sheets were stored unsealed overnight in a school office.

The implausibly high accuracy on the hardest items indicates that proctors supplied correct answers to students during the test session. The overnight storage of completed sheets, unsealed, in a school office resulted in school staff altering student answer sheets after the test session had ended. At least one of these two mechanisms was at work at Lincoln Elementary, answers fed to pupils in the room or sheets reworked once the room was empty, and perhaps both were. After the four teachers' accounts of the unsealed sheets, either the state invalidated at least some of Lincoln Elementary's fifth-grade test scores or no test scores at Lincoln Elementary were invalidated; exactly one of those two dispositions obtained, for they cannot both stand. The adjudication therefore turns on convergence: an instructional-reform account must explain the document-level signatures as well as the headline gain, and it cannot.

data.question: How does an ethics review board adjudicate between the claim that a researcher's undisclosed data manipulation reflected deliberate misconduct and the claim that it stemmed from honest error?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Honest error is classified as a form of research misconduct under federal regulations.
  • The standard of proof in research misconduct proceedings is beyond a reasonable doubt.
data.a_html:
Adjudication of such a dispute begins with the governing definition rather than with the parties' own characterizations of the conduct. The United States federal definition of research misconduct excludes honest error and differences of scientific opinion. Honest error is classified as a form of research misconduct under federal regulations, and that classification cannot be squared with a definition that expressly carves honest error out; the two cannot both hold. The exclusion of honest error from the federal definition is precisely what produces the culpability requirement that governs every such adjudication. A finding of research misconduct requires proof that the act was committed intentionally, knowingly, or recklessly, while the standard of proof in federal research misconduct proceedings is a preponderance of the evidence; a demand for proof of a culpable mental state cannot be squared with so modest an evidentiary threshold, and the two cannot both govern the same case. The standard of proof in research misconduct proceedings is beyond a reasonable doubt, and that criminal threshold cannot be squared with a preponderance of the evidence, since no single proceeding can be decided under both.

The procedural architecture of a case is built to put the question of state of mind on a documentary footing rather than leaving it to testimony. The inquiry stage determines whether an allegation has sufficient substance to warrant a full investigation, and investigation committees sequester original laboratory notebooks and raw instrument files at the outset of a case; a preliminary filter on whether any investigation is warranted rules out the seizure of the primary records before that filter has operated. Image file metadata records the dates of modification and the software used to make edits. data.question: How does a court decide whether a defendant's conduct or an intervening third party's act bears legal responsibility for a plaintiff's injury when the evidentiary record supports two incompatible accounts of the sequence of events?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation once the plaintiff establishes an injury.
  • A criminal act committed by a third party always severs the chain of causation.
data.a_html:
A court faced with two incompatible accounts of how an injury came about begins by dividing its task. Factual causation and legal causation are analysed as two separate inquiries, and that division shows what the first of them demands: the but-for test asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct. The plaintiff carries the burden of proving causation in a civil negligence action. The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation once the plaintiff establishes an injury.

The standard of proof for causation in a civil action is the balance of probabilities; that is, the reviewing court concluded that the plaintiff was required to prove causation only on the balance of probabilities, and the placing of the burden of causation on the plaintiff is precisely what shows that conclusion to be correct. The record establishes at least one of two things, and perhaps both: the stair tread was broken at the time of the plaintiff's fall, or the warning barricade had been removed from the stairway before the plaintiff's fall. Either state of affairs puts the occupier's conduct squarely within the sequence that ends in the plaintiff's injury.

That the plaintiff need prove causation to no higher a level than the balance of probabilities carries a direct consequence for where responsibility for choosing between the two versions of events lies. The trial judge resolves conflicts between irreconcilable witness accounts, and that primacy in the assessment of testimony has led appellate courts to defer to trial findings of fact absent palpable and overriding error. The practical effect is that the party who loses the factual contest at first instance faces a correspondingly narrow path on review, and the chosen narrative of the sequence of events becomes the foundation on which the legal analysis proceeds.

The second inquiry is different in kind, for it asks not whether the defendant's conduct figured in the sequence but whether responsibility should attach to it once a third party has acted. A superseding cause relieves the original defendant of liability for the resulting injury. A criminal act committed by a third party always severs the chain of causation. An intervening act that is reasonably foreseeable, by contrast with one that supersedes, leaves the defendant's liability intact. That principle indicates the outcome reached on appeal: the appellate court ultimately held that the third party's act was reasonably foreseeable and did not break the chain of causation, a holding that cannot be squared with any rule under which a third party's criminal act invariably severs the chain of causation. The defendant who creates a hazard and leaves it exposed therefore answers for the injury that follows, whatever hand last touched the scene.

data.question: How did biologists settle the dispute over whether mitochondria descend from free-living bacteria engulfed by an ancestral host cell or instead arose from the infolding of that cell's own membranes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.
  • Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria.
data.a_html:
Two rival accounts of the mitochondrion's origin were on the table for most of the twentieth century, and the means of deciding between them arrived only with molecular biology. Ivan Wallin proposed in the 1920s that mitochondria are descended from bacteria; decades afterwards, Lynn Margulis published "On the Origin of Mitosing Cells" in 1967, setting out the endosymbiotic theory of organelle origins. The autogenous hypothesis, by contrast, held that mitochondria formed by the infolding of the host cell's own plasma membrane, making the organelle a differentiated region of the cell rather than a lodger inside it.

Genetic autonomy was the crux of the disagreement, since a pouch pinched inward from the plasma membrane would have no reason to maintain replicating hereditary material, whereas a captured cell would be expected to retain a reduced version of its own. Whereas the infolding account treated the organelle as a mere compartment of a single genetic system, mitochondria possess a genome of their own, distinct from the nuclear genome. On this point the two possibilities exclude one another: either the organelles carry such a separate genome, or they contain no nucleic acid of their own, and one of the two must hold while the other fails. Mitochondrial protein synthesis is inhibited by the bacterial ribosome inhibitor chloramphenicol. Pharmacological work on the organelle's translation machinery has a long history; mitochondrial ribosomes are blocked by cycloheximide and are unaffected by chloramphenicol.

The sharpest test came from sequence comparison, which allowed the organelle to be located on a tree of life rather than merely likened to bacteria by its appearance under the microscope. Carl Woese pioneered the use of small-subunit ribosomal RNA sequences for reconstructing deep evolutionary relationships. Ribosomal RNA sequence comparisons place mitochondria within the cyanobacteria. Any cyanobacterial affiliation for the organelle cannot be squared with the signal the molecules themselves carry: comparisons of mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequences place mitochondria within the Alphaproteobacteria, among the relatives of the rickettsiae.

Gene content supplied the final piece of the argument. That mitochondria descend from a free-living bacterium taken up by an ancestral host cell is confirmed by the mitochondrial genome of Reclinomonas americana, which retains bacterial-type RNA polymerase genes. In other words, the ancestor of the mitochondrion was a prokaryotic cell acquired from outside rather than a product of the host's own membranes. Such placement within the Alphaproteobacteria is what shows the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria to be the accepted explanation in modern cell biology, with debate now confined to the identity of the partners and the order of events rather than to the fact of the symbiosis.

data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate between the claim that neighborhood disadvantage itself shapes children's later life outcomes and the claim that such outcomes merely reflect the kinds of families who end up in those neighborhoods?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18.
  • The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods randomly assigned families to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy.
data.a_html:
The dispute between neighborhood-effects researchers and their critics turns on a problem of inference rather than of measurement. Selection bias arises when families' unmeasured attributes determine which neighborhoods they enter; in other words, unmeasured parental characteristics influence which neighborhoods families move into. Faced with the familiar correlation between childhood address and adult attainment, sociologists must therefore establish that at least one of two things holds: either such unmeasured parental characteristics shape where families move, or neighborhood conditions exert a causal influence on children's adult earnings, and perhaps both hold at once. No cross-sectional association, however finely adjusted, can settle which of the two is doing the work.

Experimental design is the standard route out of this impasse, which is why the mechanics of particular programs matter so much. Either Moving to Opportunity allocated its housing vouchers to participating families by lottery, or placement in the Moving to Opportunity experimental group was determined by caseworker discretion rather than by lottery; one of these two descriptions must hold, and they cannot both hold. Allocation by lot, where it is genuinely achieved, results in randomized voucher assignment severing the link between family background and neighborhood context. That is to say, lottery-based allocation of housing vouchers makes a family's neighborhood statistically independent of its parental characteristics.

For this reason the long-run follow-up to that experiment supplies the evidence that confirms the causal claim about neighborhood conditions and children's adult earnings. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz reported that children who moved to low-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults, a pattern which shows that the Moving to Opportunity earnings gains were concentrated among children who moved after age 18. By contrast, the interim Moving to Opportunity evaluation found no significant effects of voucher receipt on adult employment or earnings, a reminder that timing and the age at which exposure occurs are integral to any causal verdict rather than incidental to it.

Observational designs enter the adjudication where experiments are unavailable or exhausted. The Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods. Families in that study were randomly assigned to neighborhoods with differing levels of collective efficacy. Whereas that Chicago effort characterized communities in terms of collective efficacy, analyses of exposure duration have reached conclusions of a quite different kind, concerning educational attainment rather than the social organization of place. Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models to estimate the effects of sustained neighborhood exposure, and those estimates show that sustained exposure to disadvantaged neighborhoods reduced the probability of high school graduation. Adjudication between the causal and the selection account thus rests, in the end, on whether a given design can render neighborhood context independent of the families who sort into it.

data.question: How do psychologists adjudicate between the claim that a failed replication reveals the original effect never existed and the claim that it reveals only an unfaithful reproduction of the original procedure?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Many Labs 2 concluded that cultural variation across sites explained most replication failures.
  • Registered Replication Reports prohibit original authors from any involvement in the replication process.
data.a_html:
The dispute begins from a datum that both parties accept. The original effect was not detected in the replication study; that is, the replication study produced no evidence of the effect reported in the original report. What is contested is not this outcome but its diagnosis, and psychologists have assembled a mixture of empirical, procedural and statistical resources for settling the question.

Logically, at least one of two things must hold of such a case, and perhaps both. The effect reported in the original study was inflated by selective reporting of analyses, or the replication procedure departed from the original procedure in a theoretically relevant respect. Whereas the first diagnosis locates the fault in the original record and its reporting practices, the second locates it in the conditions under which the effect was sought: the hidden moderator hypothesis attributes replication failure to unmeasured contextual differences between the original and replication settings. In other words, to say that the replication departed from the original in a theoretically relevant respect is to put the hidden moderator's claim in procedural terms. Adjudication therefore turns on evidence about how much setting actually matters, and here the hidden-moderator account cannot be squared with what the largest multi-site projects have measured. Many Labs 2 found that effect sizes varied little across samples and research settings. The project concluded that cultural variation across sites explained most replication failures.

A second line of adjudication is procedural rather than empirical. Daniel Kahneman proposed a "replication etiquette" obliging replicators to consult the authors of the original study, and that proposal resulted in the editorial machinery of Registered Replication Reports. Registered Replication Reports require the replication protocol to be reviewed by the original authors before data collection begins. Under this format, original authors are prohibited from any involvement in the replication process.

Statistical criteria supply a third resource, since the two diagnoses differ in what they predict about the magnitude of the effect. The small telescopes approach tests whether the true effect is too small to have been detectable by the original study's sample size; put differently, equivalence testing permits researchers to conclude that an effect is smaller than a prespecified bound. A replication that licenses such a conclusion shifts the burden onto the proponent of a moderator to name it and measure it.

The practical force of these conventions is clearest in disputed cases. Simone Schnall objected to a failed replication of her cleanliness priming study on the grounds that the replication's measures suffered from ceiling effects, and that objection led the journal's editorial review board to conclude that the ceiling-effect objection did not account for the failed cleanliness priming replication. The general lesson is that the choice between a nonexistent effect and an unfaithful reproduction stops being a matter of competing assertion only when protocols are fixed and vetted in advance, when putative moderators are measured rather than merely invoked, and when the smallest effect the original design could have detected is stated explicitly.

data.question: How do engineers adjudicate between a latent software defect and a hardware fault when a distributed database silently corrupts records, and what evidence ultimately settles the attribution?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure.
  • ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module.
data.a_html:
Adjudicating between a latent software defect and a hardware fault in a silently corrupting distributed database is a matter of pattern discrimination, and it begins with detection rather than with diagnosis. Background scrub jobs recompute stored checksums to detect silent corruption; only after such a job flags a mismatch do engineers compare the byte content of the same record across each of its replicas. The outcome of that comparison supplies the evidence that discriminates between the competing hypotheses. Byte-identical corruption on independent replicas points to a fault in the shared software path. Replica topology enters the picture as well: byte-identical corruption across replicas in separate datacenters proves independent hardware failure. By contrast, corruption isolated to a single replica on a single node points to a localized hardware fault. The question is never settled by the fact of corruption alone, but by its distribution across machines that share code yet share no silicon.

A second line of inquiry runs through the hardware telemetry gathered for the interval in which the scrub reported mismatches. ECC memory controllers log correctable single-bit error counts for each memory module. Vendors document the correction scheme in detail; ECC memory corrects all multi-bit errors within a single memory module. Those per-module records show that single-bit flips at arbitrary offsets are characteristic of DRAM faults. Engineers therefore read the counters alongside device firmware logs, looking for a module or a drive whose error rate rose in step with the first observed mismatch.

The signature recovered in the incident under review had a different shape entirely: the damaged bytes did not wander across the page but sat at predictable offsets. Corruption aligned to record and page boundaries is characteristic of a serialization defect, and that alignment showed that the storage engine's compaction code contained a latent defect which mishandled a rare offset case. Reproducing that offset case against a synthetic workload then took the argument out of the realm of inference, since the same mangled output appeared on hardware whose counters were clean.

At least one of two conditions therefore obtained: a latent defect in the compaction path, or an uncorrectable fault in the memory of node seven, and conceivably both at once. The memory module in node seven did have an uncorrectable hardware fault. Even though that module had failed outright, the post-incident review board concluded that the root cause was a latent software defect in the compaction path, because the boundary-aligned damage extended to replicas that shared no memory with node seven.

On the question of consequences, exactly one of two outcomes holds and the two cannot both be true: either every corrupted record was recoverable from backups and replica repair, or at least one corrupted record was permanently unrecoverable. What ultimately settles the attribution is the conjunction of three findings: the cross-replica byte comparison, the per-module error history, and a deterministic reproduction of the fault on hardware known to be sound.

data.question: How do scholars adjudicate whether a cultural practice shared by two widely separated societies spread from a single source or emerged independently in each?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Franz Boas rejected diffusion and explained cultural similarities solely by independent invention.
  • The age-area hypothesis holds that the region where a trait appears most recently is its center of origin.
data.a_html:
Scholars contrast diffusion from a single source with independent invention when explaining a trait shared by two distant societies, and the history of the discipline still supplies the terms in which that contrast is argued. The Kulturkreis diffusionists traced most cultural traits to a small number of originating centers, a position that cannot be squared with the unilineal evolutionists' claim that societies pass through similar stages and invent similar traits independently; the two accounts cannot both be true. The evolutionists advanced their scheme first; only afterwards did Franz Boas reject diffusion and explain cultural similarities solely by independent invention. Whereas the Kulturkreis school concentrated the origins of culture in a few favoured centers, Boas's account allowed no transmission between peoples whatever.

In practice, adjudication begins with the plausibility of transmission itself. A diffusion hypothesis requires a demonstrable route of contact between the two societies, a corridor of trade, migration or navigation along which the practice could actually have travelled. Because such a corridor must be exhibited rather than taken for granted, the absence of a trait in intervening regions weakens a diffusion claim, for a practice that moved should have left deposits along its path. The age-area hypothesis, by contrast, holds that the region where a trait appears most recently is its center of origin, and distributional reasoning of this kind has long been used to convert maps of occurrence into narratives of movement.

Distribution alone, however, does not settle the matter, since the character of the resemblance is itself diagnostic. Because convergent functional constraints can produce similar technologies in societies that never met, shared arbitrary details, such as ornament, nomenclature, taboo or ritual sequence, thereby come to carry more evidential weight for common origin than shared functional features do.

Loanwords accompanying a practice support its transmission from one society to the other. Comparative linguistics is accordingly among the instruments the problem demands, and the sound-correspondences of a borrowed term can be traced with a precision that artefact typology rarely allows.

A 2020 genomic study published in Nature reported admixture between Polynesians and Native Americans around 1200 CE, a finding that shows ancient DNA can establish population contact independently of material culture. That report came after sweet potato chronology had already framed the Pacific question as a stark either/or: either the remains recovered in Polynesia predate 1492, or every specimen recovered there postdates 1492; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. Settling that chronology, rather than any general preference for transmission or for invention, is what the Polynesian case now awaits.

data.question: How did biologists establish whether the genetic material of the cell is DNA or protein, and what reasoning settled the dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944.
  • Hershey and Chase used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage.
data.a_html:
The question of whether heredity resided in nucleic acid or in protein was settled by a chain of experiments on bacteria and on the viruses that infect them. Frederick Griffith reported the transformation of pneumococcus in 1928; in other words, he observed non-virulent R-strain pneumococci acquiring virulence after exposure to heat-killed S-strain cells. Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944, a dating that cannot be squared with a report of the same observation appearing in 1928. Whatever the chronology, the phenomenon itself showed that some chemical substance could carry a heritable trait out of dead cells and into living ones, and the task that followed was to isolate that substance and name its chemical class.

Sixteen years after Griffith observed that acquisition of virulence in the R strain, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published their identification of the transforming principle in 1944. Phoebus Levene's tetranucleotide hypothesis depicted DNA as a monotonous repeating molecule. That hypothesis caused protein to be the favoured candidate for the hereditary material among biologists before 1944.

The Avery group treated their transforming extract with proteolytic enzymes such as trypsin and chymotrypsin. By contrast, treatment of the transforming extract with deoxyribonuclease destroyed its transforming activity altogether. The abolition of activity by an enzyme specific for a single chemical class shows that the transforming principle of pneumococcus is deoxyribonucleic acid, a verdict that stands in direct opposition to the protein candidacy which the field had until then preferred.

Corroboration came from a wholly different system. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase published their bacteriophage blender experiment in 1952. Hershey and Chase labelled bacteriophage DNA with the radioisotope phosphorus-32, and as a result most of the phosphorus-32 label was recovered in the pellet of infected bacteria. Hershey and Chase labelled the bacteriophage protein coat with the radioisotope sulfur-35. They used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage; these two accounts of how the coat was marked cannot both be true. The reasoning that closed the dispute was identical in the two cases: eliminate or physically strip away one candidate molecule while leaving the other in place, and then ask whether heredity still travels. Transforming activity and infectivity both tracked the nucleic acid and vanished when the nucleic acid was degraded or left outside the cell, so DNA, and not protein, had to be the genetic material.

data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between the claim that a failed replication reflects a false original finding and the claim that it reflects unmeasured differences in method or sample, and what evidence settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Increasing the sample size of a replication reduces its statistical power to detect the original effect.
  • Many Labs 2 found that cultural setting accounted for most of the variation in effect sizes across its samples.
data.a_html:
The dispute between these two diagnoses is settled by design rather than by argument, and the large coordinated replication efforts are where the question is joined. The Reproducibility Project: Psychology attempted replications of 100 studies drawn from 2008 psychology journals. Because publication bias inflates the effect sizes reported in the original published literature, only thirty-six percent of the project's replications produced statistically significant results in the same direction as the original studies. Gilbert and colleagues argued that many Reproducibility Project replications used protocols that departed from the original studies, a contention that cannot be squared with that observed rate of concordant significant replications, since the two cannot both be true. Even granting that many replication protocols departed from the originals in this way, obtaining the original author's endorsement of the replication protocol before data collection is a standard safeguard in replication research.

Interpreting an individual failure requires separating what the published record already guarantees from what remains open. Because publication bias inflates what the literature reports in just this fashion, the original study's reported effect size exceeded the true population effect size. At least one of two conditions must therefore hold in any such case, and perhaps both of them do: that overstatement of the original estimate, or the fact that the replication differed from the original study on a variable that moderates the effect.

What breaks the deadlock is the move from post hoc explanation to prospective test. A hidden-moderator explanation becomes testable when the proposed moderator is directly manipulated in a new experiment. Registered Replication Reports coordinate a common preregistered protocol across multiple independent laboratories. Quantitative benchmarks do complementary work here. Simonsohn's small telescopes test compares the replication effect size with the effect size the original study had 33% power to detect. Increasing the sample size of a replication reduces its statistical power to detect the original effect, a claim that cannot be squared with the logic of that benchmark, for the two cannot both be true.

The sequence of the evidence is instructive: the common preregistered protocol was fixed across the participating laboratories first, and only afterwards was the pooled estimate for ego depletion reported. Whereas the hidden-moderator reading requires that the replication and the original diverged on some consequential variable, the multi-site evidence points the other way. Many Labs 2 found that variation in effect sizes across samples and settings was small relative to the size of the effects themselves. The ego depletion Registered Replication Report estimated the effect size at approximately d = 0.04. Many Labs 2 further reported that cultural setting accounted for most of the variation in effect sizes across its samples, a conclusion that cannot be squared with its finding that such variation was small relative to the size of the effects themselves; both cannot be true at once. Taken together, preregistered multi-laboratory designs and direct manipulation of the candidate moderator are what convert an unfalsifiable appeal to unmeasured differences into a claim that can be put at risk.

data.question: How do linguists adjudicate between inheritance from a common ancestor and contact-induced borrowing when two languages share a striking grammatical feature, and what evidence ultimately settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Grammatical morphology is never transferred between languages in situations of contact.
  • The shared features of the Balkan languages are inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European.
data.a_html:
When two languages share a striking grammatical feature, adjudicating between common descent and contact-induced transfer begins with the instruments used to establish relatedness in the first place. The comparative method establishes genetic relationship through regular, recurrent sound correspondences, while calquing transfers a grammatical pattern from one language to another without transferring phonological material; a diagnosis anchored in recurrent sound matches and a mode of transfer that carries no phonological material whatever cannot both be true. Each mechanism leaves a different residue in the material of the languages, and it is that residue, rather than the salience of the resemblance itself, that the analyst must weigh.

The alternatives can be put sharply. At least one of two histories must be true, and perhaps both: the shared feature was inherited by both languages from their common ancestor, or the shared feature passed from one speech community to the other through bilingual contact. That a grammatical pattern can be transplanted with none of its phonological substance, as the process described above demonstrates, is evidence for the second route, the movement of the feature across a bilingual boundary. Shared arbitrary morphological irregularities are strong evidence of descent from a common ancestor; in other words, idiosyncratic paradigm anomalies held in common by two languages point to inheritance from a shared parent language. Where such anomalies can be exhibited, they show that the feature came down to both languages from the parent rather than travelling between them.

Weighing the two histories depends further on known asymmetries in what diffuses across language boundaries. Basic vocabulary resists borrowing more strongly than cultural vocabulary. Within morphology the counts fall out thus: bound inflectional morphology is transferred between languages far less often than free lexical items. Grammatical morphology is never transferred between languages in situations of contact; that categorical exclusion cannot be squared with the gradient finding that bound inflection merely transfers less readily than free lexical material.

What ultimately settles a dispute of this kind is chronology, both internal and external. Reconstruction showing that a feature was absent in the proto-language indicates that the feature is a later innovation. Philological work has an object of its own: dated written records fix the earliest attestation of a grammatical feature in a language's history. Where the reconstructed history and the documentary record converge on a date later than the separation of the two languages, the ancestral account falls away and transfer remains the only available history.

Albanian, Romanian, and Bulgarian all place the definite article after the noun, and that common postposition shows the Balkan Sprachbund to comprise Albanian, Romanian, Greek, Bulgarian, and Macedonian. The shared features of the Balkan languages are inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European; yet that genealogical account cannot be squared with the composition of the convergence area just described, whose members are drawn from branches far too distantly related for such traits to have survived in common. Adjudication, then, rests not on the striking resemblance itself but on the joint testimony of reconstruction, dated attestation, and areal distribution.

data.question: How do scholars decide whether a shared cultural practice found in two widely separated societies spread by contact or arose independently, and what kind of finding settles such a dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue.
  • Sweet potato was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia.
data.a_html:
The choice between diffusion and independent invention is decided by the pattern of evidence rather than by the intrinsic plausibility of the trait itself. Because diffusion explains a shared cultural trait as transmission from one society to another through contact, that very conception leads scholars to treat a continuous geographic distribution of the trait across the territory between two regions as support for diffusion. Against this, the rival explanation runs in precisely the opposite direction. Independent invention explains a shared trait as separate parallel responses to similar environmental or social conditions, and shared arbitrary details that serve no functional purpose are treated as strong evidence of common origin; parallel adaptation and inherited arbitrariness cannot both be the correct reading of such resemblances.

That same evidential principle — the weight placed on arbitrary, functionless correspondences — shows why loanwords shared between the languages of two societies indicate direct contact between their speakers. Two further instruments do different kinds of work. Ancient DNA analysis can detect genomic admixture produced by contact between two populations; radiocarbon dating, by contrast, establishes the relative chronology of a trait's first appearance in each region. That chronological role cannot be squared with the fact that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue; the two accounts of the method cannot both be true.

The Polynesian sweet potato shows how a dispute of this kind is brought to a close. Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is native to tropical America. The crop was domesticated in Island Southeast Asia, a homeland that rules out an American nativity, since the plant cannot have originated in both places. Charred sweet potato remains from Mangaia in the Cook Islands were radiocarbon dated to about AD 1000, and herbarium specimens collected during early European voyages have been used to reconstruct sweet potato lineages in Polynesia; the Mangaian date and the herbarium reconstruction cannot both stand.

Some nine centuries after those tubers were charred and buried, the question of transport across the Pacific was addressed by experiment rather than by excavation. Thor Heyerdahl's 1947 Kon-Tiki raft voyage travelled from Peru to the Tuamotu Islands. A demonstration that a voyage is feasible does not establish that the transfer actually occurred. A controversy of this type is therefore closed only by a find that ties the two societies to each other directly — a dated specimen, a genome, a borrowed word — and not by a demonstration of what was merely within reach.

data.question: How did physicists adjudicate between the competing accounts of the 2011 OPERA result that neutrinos had outpaced light, and what finally settled whether the anomaly reflected new physics or an instrumental artifact?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • The CERN-to-Gran Sasso baseline used in the OPERA measurement was 450 kilometres long.
  • The OPERA anomaly was traced to an error in the geodetic survey of the baseline distance.
data.a_html:
The 2011 anomaly was adjudicated in the way such disputes usually are: by interrogating every link in the measurement chain and by asking what else would have to be true if the result stood. The neutrinos studied by OPERA were produced in the CNGS beam at CERN. The flight path between the CERN source and the OPERA detector spanned about 730 kilometres. The CERN-to-Gran Sasso baseline used in the OPERA measurement was 450 kilometres long, and that length cannot be squared with a separation of some 730 kilometres, since no single flight path can have both extents.

OPERA reported in September 2011 that neutrinos arrived roughly 60 nanoseconds earlier than light would have, and the collaboration released that measurement as an arXiv preprint and invited independent scrutiny instead of claiming a discovery; a timing excess asserted that definitely and a refusal to claim the discovery it would constitute cannot both stand. The early-arrival figure, together with the choice to circulate it for outside checking rather than to proclaim a discovery, is what prompted the first theoretical reckoning: because a 60-nanosecond head start had been put into open circulation in precisely that provisional form, particle theorists set about deriving what such a beam would have to do on its way through the rock.

The OPERA timing chain depended on GPS satellite synchronisation between CERN and Gran Sasso. The baseline distance was fixed by geodetic surveying to an accuracy of about 20 centimetres. The OPERA anomaly was traced to an error in the geodetic survey of the baseline distance, a diagnosis that cannot be squared with a separation pinned down to roughly a fifth of a metre, for a distance known that precisely cannot be mistaken by the tens of metres a 60-nanosecond head start would require. By contrast, OPERA disclosed two faults in its timing equipment in February 2012, a disclosure that placed the suspect element in the apparatus rather than in the surveyed geometry.

Andrew Cohen and Sheldon Glashow argued that superluminal neutrinos would lose energy by emitting electron-positron pairs in flight. The ICARUS experiment observed no sign of the in-flight energy loss predicted by Cohen and Glashow. The weight of the case, in the end, lay with repetition of the measurement itself. The February disclosures came first, and the decisive remeasurements followed in the weeks after. ICARUS reported in March 2012 a neutrino time-of-flight consistent with light propagation, and that result confirms that the OPERA, ICARUS, LVD and Borexino experiments all reported neutrino velocities compatible with the speed of light. In other words, the neutrinos crossed the baseline in the same time that light would have taken, and the anomaly belonged to the instrument rather than to nature.

data.question: How do forensic engineers establish whether a bridge collapse originated in a design deficiency or in subsequent construction and maintenance practice when the design firm and the contractor each attribute the failure to the other?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.
  • The probable cause was overloading of the deck by parked construction equipment.
data.a_html:
Attributing a bridge failure to design or to execution is a problem of reconciling the physical record of the structure with the paper record of the decisions made about it, and the Florida International University walkway offers a model of how the two are brought together. When the pedestrian bridge collapsed onto an open roadway during construction, the gravity of the event led the National Transportation Safety Board to take charge of the federal investigation. The investigators' first obligation was to establish precisely what the structure was doing in the period leading up to the failure. Structural cracking was documented at the north end of the span in the days before the collapse, and workers were re-tensioning post-tensioning rods in a diagonal member at the moment the span fell; cracking already recorded at the north end rules out re-tensioning work being underway in that diagonal as the structure came down.

Out of that record two candidate explanations arise, and at least one of them is true, perhaps both: the contractor left the span unshored during the re-tensioning operation; the design drawings understated the shear demand at the critical truss node. The federal inquiry so constituted led directly to the principal technical exercise of the case. Forensic engineers rebuilt the structural model using finite element analysis to recompute member capacities. Tensile testing of recovered reinforcing steel showed that it met the specified yield strength. Those recomputed capacities confirm the understatement of shear demand in the drawings. By contrast with the reinforcing steel, the concrete as placed was deficient: concrete cylinder tests showed compressive strengths forty percent below specification.

The documentary and regulatory record runs parallel to this laboratory work. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration issued citations to the construction contractor after the collapse. The peer reviewer's scope of work omitted a capacity check of the critical nodal region. The citations issued against the contractor show that the span was indeed left without shoring while the rods were being re-tensioned.

Only against an assembled record of this kind can a probable cause be stated, and the competing versions must then be measured against one another. The probable cause was overloading of the deck by parked construction equipment. The probable cause of the collapse was errors in the design firm's load and capacity calculations; overloading by parked equipment and miscalculation of loads and capacities cannot both have brought the span down. That is to say, the failure is attributable to the engineer of record miscalculating structural demand and resistance. The gap left in the peer reviewer's scope indicates exactly that attribution, since the one independent check capable of catching the error at the node was never carried out. Where the design firm and the contractor each point at the other, it is this interlocking of recomputed mechanics, material testing and the audit trail of review that decides between them.

data.question: How do clinicians establish whether a patient's sudden muscle weakness originates in the nervous system or in the muscle tissue itself, and what evidence ultimately settles the matter?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies.
  • Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres.
  • Motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre.
data.a_html:
The first discrimination is clinical, and it rests on the distribution of the deficit and on what accompanies it. Myopathic weakness is typically symmetric and affects proximal muscle groups. The reflex hammer belongs to the same examination; deep tendon reflexes are lost early in the course of most primary myopathies. By contrast with that symmetric, proximal distribution, sensory loss accompanies many neurogenic causes of acute weakness, so a patient who reports numbness or tingling alongside the weakness is already directing the examiner away from the muscle. Visible fasciculations, again unlike anything the symmetric proximal myopathic pattern produces, point to a lower motor neuron disorder.

Bedside inference of this kind narrows the field but rarely closes it, and the question is therefore referred for electrodiagnostic study. Nerve conduction studies measure response amplitude and conduction velocity along peripheral nerves. Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres; yet a technique that stimulates a nerve trunk and times the travel of the evoked response cannot at the same moment be sampling single fibres at rest, and measuring conduction along the nerve and registering spontaneous activity in resting fibres cannot both be what the method does. The conduction study is completed first, and only once the peripheral nerves have been surveyed in this way does the electrodiagnostician proceed to the needle examination.

Because needle electromyography records motor unit action potentials from within the muscle, long-duration, high-amplitude polyphasic motor unit potentials come to indicate chronic denervation with reinnervation. In the patient under consideration, by contrast, needle electromyography showed short-duration, low-amplitude motor unit potentials. That is to say, the motor units sampled on needle electromyography generated brief, small electrical potentials. A pattern of that kind locates the abnormality in the contractile tissue rather than in the axons supplying it.

Serum creatine kinase is released into the bloodstream when muscle fibre membranes are damaged, and it is precisely for that reason that motor neuron disease characteristically raises serum creatine kinase above 10,000 units per litre. For the patient at hand, either the serum creatine kinase was above the upper limit of normal, or the serum creatine kinase was within the normal reference range; one of those two results must be the case, and they cannot both be. Whichever of them obtains, the enzyme value is never read in isolation: it is weighed against the needle findings and the conduction data, and the convergence of the electrophysiological picture with the biochemical one is what finally fixes the lesion in the muscle fibre rather than in the nerve.

data.question: How do scholars adjudicate a disputed attribution of an anonymous literary work, and what settles the matter when stylometric evidence points one way while documentary records point another?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays.
  • Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote A Funeral Elegy.
data.a_html:
Attribution scholarship proceeds by assembling several kinds of evidence and asking which hypothesis about authorship best accounts for all of them. Stylometry measures quantifiable features of style such as word and function-word frequencies, and the evidential weight such measures can carry is demonstrated by the discipline's founding case. Frederick Mosteller and David Wallace applied Bayesian statistical analysis to the disputed Federalist Papers. Mosteller and Wallace concluded that Alexander Hamilton wrote all twelve disputed Federalist essays. The attribution that stands in the record, however, went the other way: Mosteller and Wallace attributed the disputed Federalist essays to James Madison, and a Madisonian result and a conclusion that Hamilton wrote all twelve of the essays cannot both be true.

Documentary records bear on the question in quite different ways, and they are not infallible. Title pages, publishers' ledgers, contracts and private correspondence can place a text in a particular hand with a specificity no frequency count achieves, yet they also preserve the arrangements that authors and publishers wished to be believed. Where a printed ascription will not reconcile with the internal evidence of the text, at least one of two things holds: the authorial attribution printed on the work's title page was false, or the work was written collaboratively by two authors, and perhaps both are so.

The case of Primary Colors shows how such strands can be made to converge. Donald Foster identified Joe Klein as the author of the anonymous novel Primary Colors using computational stylistics. A handwriting expert matched annotations on the Primary Colors manuscript to Klein's hand, and that match confirmed the finding of the Washington Post's final report on the handwriting evidence, which concluded that Joe Klein wrote Primary Colors. Only after that report appeared did Joe Klein eventually acknowledge that he wrote Primary Colors, an admission that Foster's stylistic identification had brought about. Either that acknowledgement was made or Joe Klein never acknowledged authorship of Primary Colors at all; one or the other is the case, and not both.

Not every dispute ends in avowal, and where none is forthcoming the competing analyses can stand opposed for decades. A Funeral Elegy, printed in 1612 over the initials W.S., is the standard instance. Gilles Monsarrat argued that John Ford wrote A Funeral Elegy. Brian Vickers concluded that Thomas Middleton wrote the poem. Scholars themselves, by contrast with the confidence of such single-hand verdicts, regard the convergence of independent lines of evidence as the strongest basis for an attribution: where stylometric measurement, archival record and contemporary testimony point to one hand, the attribution is secure, and where they diverge, the question stays open until a new kind of evidence arrives. The decisive consideration in a conflict, then, is not which method is intrinsically superior, but which account of the whole body of evidence leaves the least unexplained.

data.question: How do researchers adjudicate between the competing claims that persistent gender disparities in STEM fields stem from differential socialization or from institutional gatekeeping, and what evidence has shifted scholarly consensus?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Differences in average mathematical ability account for the underrepresentation of women among academic scientists.
  • Title IX of the United States Education Amendments was enacted in 1992.
data.a_html:
Adjudication between socialization accounts and gatekeeping accounts of persistent gender disparities in STEM begins with the recognition that even the descriptive baseline is disputed. Either women earn a majority of United States bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences, or they earn a minority of them: one of these two descriptions must be correct, and they cannot both be correct. The two explanatory traditions differ chiefly in where they locate the decisive mechanism along the educational and professional pipeline. On the current evidence, at least one of the following holds, and perhaps both hold together: parents give girls less encouragement toward mathematics than they give boys, and hiring and promotion committees in academic science apply evaluation criteria that disadvantage women candidates.

Deciding between these loci requires research designs that hold candidate quality constant while varying only the applicant's apparent sex. Goldin and Rouse found that blind auditions raised women's chances of advancing in symphony orchestra hiring rounds, work that came earlier than the faculty-evaluation experiments considered below. Researchers use correspondence experiments with randomly assigned applicant names to separate discrimination from applicant differences. Moss-Racusin and colleagues published a 2012 randomized experiment on science faculty evaluations in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. The 2012 lab-manager experiment drew on faculty of both sexes, and male and female faculty alike displayed comparable levels of bias against the female applicant.

By contrast with that uniformity of bias across evaluator sex, the strategy of randomly assigning applicant names resulted in a further body of work, most prominently Williams and Ceci's report of a national experiment in which faculty preferred hypothetical women candidates for tenure-track positions at a two-to-one ratio. The explanatory field is also constrained from a different direction. Differences in average mathematical ability account for the underrepresentation of women among academic scientists. A National Academies consensus report determined that harassment and hostile climate, rather than ability differences, drive substantial attrition of women from academic science, and that determination cannot be squared with the account resting on average ability differences; the two explanations cannot both stand.

The consensus report's determination is itself the evidential basis for a narrower claim about the mechanism of departure. Sexual harassment is a documented driver of women's attrition from academic science careers, and that documented loss of trained scientists led the National Science Foundation to fund institutional-change grants aimed at women's advancement in academic science through its ADVANCE program. Chronology matters here as well: Title IX of the United States Education Amendments was enacted in 1992, which is to say before the funding program just described began awarding its grants. The upshot for scholarly consensus is that the socialization and gatekeeping accounts are not adjudicated by appeal to aggregate participation figures, which admit of competing descriptions, but by experimental and institutional evidence bearing directly on evaluation and climate. Randomized manipulations of applicant identity isolate the behavior of gatekeepers from any differences in the candidates themselves, and consensus reviews of attrition locate the mechanism in the conditions women encounter after entry rather than in the dispositions they bring to it.

data.question: How do sociologists adjudicate whether poor neighborhoods themselves shape residents' later life outcomes or whether the families who end up in such neighborhoods already differ in ways that produce those outcomes?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Sibling fixed-effects designs remove all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.
  • Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery.
data.a_html:
Sociologists approach the neighborhood question as a problem of causal identification rather than of portraiture, and the field's answer has been assembled out of successive designs, each imposing a stricter standard on how a family came to live where it lives. The earliest generation of this work was devoted to measuring the social properties of places and relating them to outcomes recorded in those same places. Robert Sampson's Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods, and those measurements show that higher collective efficacy was associated with lower rates of neighborhood violence.

Patrick Sharkey has documented multigenerational exposure to high-poverty neighborhoods among Black American families. That pattern of inherited place indicates that observational neighborhood studies are vulnerable to omitted variable bias from unmeasured parental traits, since the same families reappear in the same disadvantaged settings generation after generation. Precisely because unmeasured parental traits distort such estimates, Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting to address time-varying confounding of neighborhood exposure. By contrast, sibling fixed-effects designs compare siblings whose childhoods were spent in neighborhoods of differing quality. Because every comparison is drawn within a single family, that design removes all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.

Housing policy supplied leverage of a different kind, since the allocation of a scarce benefit by lottery converts the question of selection into a question of who was offered a chance to move. The Gautreaux program relocated Chicago public housing residents under a court-ordered desegregation remedy, and the Moving to Opportunity demonstration was mounted afterward. That demonstration randomly assigned housing voucher offers to low-income families in five U.S. cities, and as a result researchers were able to use the randomized voucher offer as an instrument for subsequent exposure to neighborhood poverty. Chetty, Hendren, and Katz found that children who moved to lower-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults.

The administrative details of that demonstration govern what can be inferred from it. Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery, a recruitment arrangement that cannot be squared with the confinement of randomized voucher offers to five metropolitan areas. Its enrollment structure admits exactly one of two possibilities: either the demonstration included a randomly assigned control group that received no new housing voucher, or every family enrolled in Moving to Opportunity received an experimental housing voucher; one of the two held, and they cannot both have held. Adjudication therefore turns on a single criterion, namely whether a given design makes neighborhood exposure independent of the family characteristics that would otherwise produce the outcome under study.

The earliest generation of this work was devoted to measuring the social properties of places and relating them to outcomes recorded in those same places. Robert Sampson's Project on Human Development in Chicago Neighborhoods measured collective efficacy across Chicago neighborhoods, and those measurements show that higher collective efficacy was associated with lower rates of neighborhood violence.

That pattern of inherited place indicates that observational neighborhood studies are vulnerable to omitted variable bias from unmeasured parental traits, since the same families reappear in the same disadvantaged settings generation after generation. Precisely because unmeasured parental traits distort such estimates, Wodtke, Harding, and Elwert applied marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting to address time-varying confounding of neighborhood exposure. By contrast, sibling fixed-effects designs compare siblings whose childhoods were spent in neighborhoods of differing quality. Because every comparison is drawn within a single family, that design removes all unobserved confounding, including factors that change over time within a family.

Housing policy supplied leverage of a different kind, since the allocation of a scarce benefit by lottery converts the question of selection into a question of who was offered a chance to move. The Gautreaux program relocated Chicago public housing residents under a court-ordered desegregation remedy, and the Moving to Opportunity demonstration was mounted afterward. That demonstration randomly assigned housing voucher offers to low-income families in five U.S. cities, and as a result researchers were able to use the randomized voucher offer as an instrument for subsequent exposure to neighborhood poverty. What that instrumented comparison shows is the result reported by Chetty, Hendren, and Katz: children who moved to lower-poverty neighborhoods before age 13 earned more as adults.

The administrative details of that demonstration govern what can be inferred from it. Moving to Opportunity recruited families in all fifty states through a national lottery, a recruitment arrangement that cannot be squared with the confinement of randomized voucher offers to five metropolitan areas. Its enrollment structure admits exactly one of two possibilities: either the demonstration included a randomly assigned control group that received no new housing voucher, or every family enrolled in Moving to Opportunity received an experimental housing voucher; one of the two held, and they cannot both have held. Adjudication therefore turns on a single criterion, namely whether a given design makes neighborhood exposure independent of the family characteristics that would otherwise produce the outcome under study.

data.question: How did chemists establish whether the loss of mass in combustion reflected the escape of a substance from the burning body or the absorption of something from the air, and what settled the dispute?
data.facts_html:
Take as given: the following claims made in these answers are false.
  • Lavoisier's calcination trials were carried out in open crucibles standing in the free atmosphere.
  • Henry Cavendish discovered oxygen in 1766 by heating red calx of mercury.
data.a_html:
The question of what is lost and what is gained in burning was, for the better part of a century, a dispute about the direction of a transfer. Georg Ernst Stahl formulated the phlogiston theory in the early eighteenth century, and on his account combustion was a giving off: a burning body released a material substance called phlogiston into the air. Whereas that doctrine made the burning body the donor, Jean Rey had argued in 1630 that calcined tin gained weight by taking up matter from the air, and it was only after Stahl's system had become the common property of chemists that this contrary suggestion was seriously revived. Rey's conjecture, in any case, preceded by nearly a century and a half the experiment that would decide between the two accounts.

Lavoisier heated tin in a hermetically sealed glass retort. There was no change in the total mass of the sealed retort after the metal had been calcined inside it. Lavoisier stated the principle that the total mass of matter is conserved in a chemical change, offering it as a general axiom of his chemistry. The balance had more to tell. When Lavoisier broke the seal of the retort after heating, air rushed into the vessel, and that inrush shows that the weight gained by the metal equalled the weight of air lost from the sealed vessel.

A difficulty attends the usual description of this work. Lavoisier's calcination trials were carried out in open crucibles standing in the free atmosphere; but a crucible standing open to the surrounding air cannot be squared with the heating of the tin in a hermetically sealed glass retort, since one and the same trial cannot have been both closed against the air and exposed to it.

Joseph Priestley obtained a new gas in 1774 by heating mercuric oxide with a burning lens, and as a result he called that gas dephlogisticated air. Henry Cavendish discovered oxygen in 1766 by heating red calx of mercury, and this rules out the first procurement of the gas from the mercury calx having come eight years later at Priestley's hands: the discovery cannot belong to Cavendish in 1766 and also be the work of 1774.

The outcome admits of just two descriptions, of which exactly one must hold and not both. Either phlogiston theory was ultimately retained as the accepted account of combustion, or — even though the gas drawn from mercuric oxide was christened dephlogisticated air, in the very idiom of the older doctrine — phlogiston theory was ultimately abandoned in favour of the oxygen theory of combustion. The weighings in closed vessels, rather than any single polemic, are what made the choice between them unavoidable.
